newsitem.title: USA: LPC - Allied Waste taps banks for $1.225 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Allied Waste taps banks for $1.225 bln loan.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 19 (LPC) - Allied Waste Industries Inc has tapped Goldman Sachs & Co Inc, Credit Suisse and Citibank to lead a $1.225 billion, senior secured bank loan, bank sources said.
The loan will fund in part Allied's roughly $1.5 billion acquisition of the solid waste management operations of Laidlaw Inc, according to banking sources.

Goldman and Citibank also have provided a "highly confident" letter for a $475 million senior subordinated debt offering to help finance the transaction, sources added. The letter offers to provide the financing but does not guarantee the deal will be consummated, they said.

The senior bank debt will comprise $250 million in revolving credit, $475 million in an amortizing term loan and $500 million in amortization extended loans (AXELs), which are term loans with nominal call protection, bankers said.
Goldman has structured several of its recent bank deals according to its AXELs format, according to lenders.
The revolving credit and amortizing term loans are priced at 250 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR), bankers said.
The three AXELs, which run 6.5, 7.5 and 8.5 years, are priced at 275, 300 and 325 basis points over LIBOR, respectively, bankers added.
Goldman served as advisor to Allied Waste on the transaction, which is expected to close in January 1997, sources said.
